prompt.content:
You are analyzing the evaluation of one candidate change to a 3D-IC physical design flow.
Hypothesis of the change: The parent relaxes the *global* density weight but the per-bin density penalty is still driven by a single scalar `density_weight`; the TNS cost comes from a few over-dense bins forcing detours. Scaling the density weight per-bin (using the preconditioner's per-region `density_weight` vector) so already-congested regions get relatively more pressure while light regions relax would reduce detours and moderate violations broadly without changing the global balance.
Rule-based digest:
total=-inf robust(mean-std)=-inf min_case=-inf all_valid=False
  failures: bp_fe-ng45/1001:stage timeout; bp_fe-ng45/1002:legalization overlap; bp_fe-ng45/1003:KeyError in partition; bp-ng45/1001:legalization overlap; bp-ng45/1002:HBT min-spacing violation; bp-ng45/1003:legalization overlap
Write <=120 words. If some runs are INVALID (failures listed), first say what kind of failure it is (legality / crash / timeout) and whether it looks systematic (all seeds of a case) or sporadic - an invalid candidate says nothing about the hypothesis itself; suggest how to make the same idea legal. Otherwise: (1) did the hypothesis hold? (2) which case/metric moved and plausible mechanism, (3) one concrete next-step suggestion. No preamble.

response: Invalid: mixed legality (legalization overlap, HBT min-spacing), crash (KeyError in partition), and timeout failures. Systematic across all seeds of both bp_fe-ng45 and bp-ng45 cases, so the candidate says nothing about the hypothesis. Likely the per-bin density vector is malformed or misindexed (KeyError) and over-aggressive per-region pressure drives overlaps/spacing violations. To make it legal: validate the per-region `density_weight` vector shape/indexing against bins, clamp per-bin scaling to a bounded range, and add a legality-repair/rollback guard before evaluating.
